SATOM 1.4.0

A fleet metrics store with Analytics boards and period reports, signed offline update packages, separate SATOM and Device health pages, and a move to the Elastic License 2.0.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-08-05 · All releases

In short#

This release changes how SATOM measures the fleet:

  • Metrics store. Metrics are now collected once per device into a local time-series store.
  • Analytics boards compare many devices on one chart over up to 90 days.
  • Reports. Daily, weekly and monthly summaries are kept as reports.
  • Health pages. Fleet health is split into SATOM health (the installation) and Device health (the appliances).

Nodes with no internet access can now be updated with signed offline update packages. The device configuration history moves out of git into a dedicated store. SATOM's licence changes to the Elastic License 2.0.

Administrators must take one manual step after upgrading to close a security issue. See Before you upgrade.

What's new#

Health pages#

SATOM health and Device health are now two pages#

Fleet health used to cover both the appliances and SATOM's own installation, and had to hide half of itself in every product ADOM. It is now two pages, nested under Fleet health:

  • SATOM health answers is this installation healthy?: HA nodes, database, services, redundancy and encryption in transit. It is available only in the Global ADOM, because it shows node names and infrastructure addresses. Product ADOMs cannot open it at all.
  • Device health answers are the appliances healthy?: device cards, capacity limits and health alerts.

More services watched#

The metrics store service now appears in the Services & redundancy list. Before, it could stop while every light on the panel stayed green. The web server, the reconciler and the update watcher were added too. Services that are meant to be idle on a given node are deliberately left off, because a check that always complains is a check people learn to ignore.

Appliance HA state from the harvested data#

The Device HA clusters panel said "No HA clusters registered" even though the hourly sweep had collected HA data for every appliance. It now shows one row per appliance: the mode, group and virtual IP, and the evidence behind the verdict.

  • Clustered only with peer evidence, such as a heartbeat device, a group name, a peer address or more than one node. The mode field alone is not enough.
  • Unknown, never standalone, without data. A device with no HA data is shown as unknown.

Metrics and analytics#

A fleet metrics store#

SATOM now collects metrics with one request per device and collector, and keeps them in a local time-series store on the node. At the target fleet size (60 FortiWeb, 30 FortiADC and 10 FortiAnalyzer, each with about 750 policies), the store holds three months at full detail in about 8 GB. The old per-probe design would have needed about 450 GB for hourly averages only.

  • Collection page. It lists every collection target with its own interval, which you can edit, and the result of its last run.
  • Expensive collectors run less often. Collectors that work per policy run less frequently, and only against the busiest policies.
  • New scheduled action. It runs the collection.

Collection starts when you save a device#

When you create or edit an appliance, or add a cluster member, its metrics collectors are created right away. Before, they appeared only on the next collection run, which on an installation with no scheduled collection meant never.

  • Parked and retired devices are skipped.
  • A problem creating collectors can no longer stop the device from being saved.
  • The Collection page also lists every device that has no collection targets and why. At this release a FortiAnalyzer has none yet, and saying so is better than staying silent.

Analytics boards#

A new page under Monitoring → Analytics puts many devices and metrics on one chart, over windows of up to 90 days.

  • Panel types: line, area, bar, stat, gauge, heatmap, table and availability strip.
  • Panel options: a min/max band, threshold lines, a second metric, comparison with the previous period, drag to reorder, a time range per panel, and optional auto-refresh.
  • Three built-in boards: Fleet overview, Traffic & sessions and Service health. To change one, duplicate it and edit the copy.
  • Panels pick their probes by rule: metric, devices and a name match. A probe recreated by Discover, or a newly added appliance, joins the panel without any edit.
  • Instant, even with devices off. Boards read the history SATOM already keeps, so they open instantly and still work with every appliance powered off.

Panels that query the metrics store#

Panels gain a third way to choose what they show: a query against the metrics store, which is the only option that works with tens of thousands of series.

  • Checked before saving. A query is run against the store before it is saved.
  • Errors are shown as errors. A failing query shows an error, not an empty chart.
  • Gaps stay gaps. Missing data is never filled in.
  • New built-in board: Fleet metrics (store).

Collection cadence#

A probe only runs when its own interval has passed and the monitoring sweep comes round. Its real rhythm can therefore be slower than its setting says: a 5-minute probe under a 3-minute sweep actually runs every 6 minutes. Analytics → Collection cadence lists every probe's set interval and real interval, and flags each one that differs. With no sweep scheduled, it shows no rhythm at all rather than a guess.

Monitoring reports#

A new page under Monitoring → Reports keeps daily, weekly and monthly summaries.

  • What a report contains: availability, min/average/95th percentile/peak for each metric, threshold breaches, drift events (daemon restarts, interface changes), an incident timeline, and the change since the previous period.
  • Fleet section. Reports also include a section from the metrics store: min/average/max per device and metric, policies that were down, and collectors that failed.
  • Stored, not recalculated. Reports are kept as they were written. Detailed data ages out over time, so a report rebuilt months later would quietly use coarser data.
  • Sharing. View reports in the console, export them as JSON, CSV or text, or send them by email using your existing mail settings. They can also be uploaded to the external backup server.
  • Recurring reports use a new scheduled action. You choose the period, whether to email it and how many to keep. As with all automations, nothing is scheduled for you. The Reports page tells you which periods are scheduled and which are not, so an empty list cannot be mistaken for "nothing happened".

Updating SATOM#

Offline update packages#

You can now update a node that has no route to the internet or the code repository. Download a signed package, upload it in Settings → Software Update, and apply it.

  • Self-contained. The package carries the application and all the libraries it needs, at about a quarter of the size of the offline install bundle.
  • Preflight first. Before anything is applied, a preflight checks the signature and shows what will happen: the version change, library changes, the Python version match, disk space and whether the upgrade path is valid.
  • Safe to apply. Applying takes a database backup, installs the update, restarts SATOM, and rolls back automatically if the health check fails.
  • From the shell too. A node without a browser can apply a package from the operator console.

Package trust#

A node accepts a package only if it is signed by a key that the node's administrator has placed on the node.

  • The vendor's key ships with SATOM. It is a public key, which can only check signatures, so publishing it is safe.
  • Your own keys. You can add your own keys and sign your own packages without depending on the vendor.
  • Signing stays off the node. The private signing key never needs to be on a managed node.
  • Operator console commands show, add and remove keys, and check that updates are set up correctly.

Operator console: work that exists only on this node#

The git check in the operator console now lists anything that exists only on this node: changed files (by name), changes not yet sent to the main repository, saved backup copies of earlier changes, and files git does not track.

  • What raises the grade. Only changed files and unsent changes do. Untracked files are listed but not graded, because they are normal on a primary node.
  • No main repository configured. The count of unsent changes says cannot tell, not zero.
  • A report, not a block. This exists because a routine update once wiped another person's unsaved work. It reports the risk; it does not stop anyone.

Release notes on the public site#

The public site now has a Releases section: a list of every version with its date and headlines, and one page per version. Everything on these pages comes from the changelog, and the current release badge comes from the version SATOM is built from, so the site cannot fall out of step. The vendor's firmware known-issues document was renamed on the site, so there are no longer two different documents called "Release notes".

Licence change: Elastic License 2.0#

SATOM's licence changed from Apache-2.0 to the Elastic License 2.0. This applies to the whole project, including the versions published before (1.0 to 1.3.5).

  • What you may still do: use, modify and run SATOM inside your own organisation, in production and for commercial purposes, on as many nodes as you like, at no cost.
  • What you may no longer do:
  • offer SATOM to third parties as a hosted or managed service (this needs a commercial licence)
  • work around licence key features
  • remove licensing notices
  • Copies you already have: a copy you received before the change keeps the Apache-2.0 terms it came with.
  • Source-available. SATOM is now described as source-available, not open source, everywhere it is published, and the published release history was updated to match.
  • Third-party notices. The notice file now names the third-party components SATOM ships, with their own licences, and says those terms still apply: the metrics store, the certificate (ACME) client, and the charting and page-layout libraries.

What changes for you#

  • Collection moved from Monitoring to Administrator, next to Capacity Limits. The other Monitoring pages show measurements; this one configures how measuring happens, and changing it needs configuration write permission. The enable/disable control on that page is now a proper button.
  • The device configuration history left git. Device configuration snapshots now go to a dedicated store on the node, where an unchanged configuration takes no extra space and how long history is kept is set by a policy.
  • History, comparison and restore stay in System Backup & Restore.
  • Snapshots are copied to the standby, included in backup bundles and sent to the external backup server.
  • The hourly git publishing of device configurations is retired, and so is the scheduled repository bundle action. You can still bundle the code repository by hand.
  • Git still holds the application code, and the way you update SATOM is unchanged.

Fixed#

  • A missing service was shown as a failed one. A service that is simply not installed now shows as neutral. A stopped service that should be running is still reported.
  • Security: a path to administrator rights through the update process. The privileged update process ran a script that the unprivileged service account could change. Someone who took over the web application could have used it to run code as administrator. This was present in every release since 1.2. The update process now runs from a protected copy owned by the administrator. See Before you upgrade: updating alone does not fix existing nodes.
  • Large uploads failed with an unexplained web server error. The web server's upload limit is now 400 MB, matching SATOM's own limit, so valid update packages are accepted.
  • The unread count on the bell floated off the bell and overlapped the user menu. It now sits on the bell, follows your custom theme colours, and all four top-bar buttons are the same height.
  • The installer could stop silently at a prompt when its answers were supplied by a script that gave fewer answers than there were questions. It now stops with a message naming the question that was not answered.
  • The installer never installed the metrics store. A fresh node had the analytics pages and the collection action but no store behind them, and an air-gapped node had no way to get it.
  • The installer now installs the store from the bundle, or downloads a fixed version and checks it.
  • All offline bundles carry the store, and a bundle cannot be built without it.
  • Only the free edition of the store is accepted.
  • Release pages repeated the same heading several times, which made one version look like several releases. The changelog sections were merged without changing any entry.

Before you upgrade#

  • After upgrading, close the update-process security gap by hand. Updating alone does not fix it. As root, run satom execute reinstall runner (or re-run the installer), then confirm with satom diagnose updates.
  • Check the new licence terms if you offer SATOM to others as a hosted or managed service. That use now needs a commercial licence.

Under the hood#

  • Panels that combine several probes now draw them all at the same level of detail, so series from different resolutions are never mixed on one axis.
  • The shipped web pages carry their own copies of their charting and layout files, so they display correctly on an isolated management network.
